```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>", fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5, fig.path="fig/")
library(CEClust)
```

# From observations to a collection of partitions

A CEC diagram describes the partitions obtained while varying a density
ceiling `C` and an entropy weight `lambda`. The aim is to inspect organizations
that remain reproducible under optimization randomness and resampling.
The result can contain several distinct partitions, rather than one selected
number of groups.

This guide uses the numeric Gaussian EM-bank engine without BIC, then reuses
the same banks with the BIC order penalty. The displayed data are simulated;
the small computational budget is for learning the interface.

## Prepare the observations

```{r data}
set.seed(12)
X <- cbind(x=c(rnorm(30,-2,0.5),rnorm(30,2,0.5)),
           y=rnorm(60,sd=0.5))
plot(X, pch=19, col="#334E68", asp=1, main="Observed measurements")
```

Rows are observations. Keep only the variables to be used in fitting; external
group labels can be supplied later as display information. Numeric engines
require complete finite data. Neither this call nor the generic fitting
function standardizes the columns. If standardization or PCA is intended,
perform it first and record the transformation. Changing units changes the
meaning of a numerical density ceiling.

## Fit a single cell

```{r single}
fit <- CECclassif(X, C=1, lambda=0.8,
  optimization="em_bank", penalty="none",
  optimizer_control=list(Rmax=3,Ninit=2,max_iter=30,seed=4))
table(fit$clusters)
c(REO=fit$REO, objective=fit$objective)
```

Here EM fits orders one to three, with two starts per order, under `Cmax=1`.
MAP gives hard candidate partitions. Empty MAP groups are removed and the
hard group parameters are re-estimated under `C=1`. The minimum hard CEC score
among the candidates supplies `fit$clusters`. The soft likelihood is used to
generate candidates, not to rank the final hard partitions.

`optimization="cem"` selects a hard CEM search instead. Both optimizers can
use `penalty="none"` or `penalty="bic"`. The method and penalty are independent
choices. A finite EM bank is an approximation, and a CEM run is a local search.

## Evaluate a grid and repeat the algorithm

```{r grid}
g <- CECfitBoundGrid(Z=X,
  C_grid=c(0.2,0.5,1), lambda_grid=c(0.6,1,1.5),
  optimization="em_bank", penalty="none",
  k0=3, B=3, algo_seed=14, n_cores=1,
  optimizer_control=list(Rmax=3,Ninit=2,Cmax=1,max_iter=30),
  rsi_policy="all",
  stab_algo_threshold=0.85, rsi_threshold=0.95, sat_threshold=0)
s <- CECsummariseGrid(g)
s[,c("C","lambda","REO","sat","stab_algo","stab_boot","rsi","keep")]
```

`k0` is the number L of complete executions on the original observations;
`B` is the number of bootstrap executions. One execution builds its own bank
with `Rmax * Ninit` attempted EM starts, then evaluates that bank on the whole
grid. Thus initializations and diagnostic repetitions have different roles.
In this example there are three original and three bootstrap banks, each
with six attempted starts.

The CEM grid engine instead searches separately at each cell of each execution.
The two routes share the scoring and diagnostic conventions. The coordinates
supplied here remain fixed. Set `grid_strategy="adaptive"` to extend the
window and refine its boundaries automatically; `?CECadaptiveDiagram` explains
the integrated rules. The optimizer and penalty remain independent choices.

```{r diagram}
par(oma=c(0,0,0,4))  # room for the rejection legend
CECplotGrid(g, main="Composite entropy: supplied grid",
  reo_col=c("#0072B2","#D55E00","#009E73"))
```

The legend distinguishes group count and diagnostic rejection. A cell is
retained here when algorithmic stability is above 0.85, RSI is above 0.95,
and saturation is zero. These are user-set diagnostic requirements, not
calibrated confidence levels.

Algorithmic stability averages the three distinct pairs of original runs.
Bootstrap stability averages all nine original-bootstrap pairs. Bootstrap
outputs are projected onto the original observations, so all label vectors
refer to the same rows. Each execution retains its own winner; the best pooled
partition is not substituted into these comparisons.

RSI divides bootstrap stability by algorithmic stability. It can exceed one.
Saturation is the fraction of observations in groups whose density constraint
is active. It reports sensitivity to a concentration ceiling, not an absence
of structure. A high agreement dominated by one large group can also hide
variation in a few observations; inspect sizes and allocations.

By default, the grid rejects a point if the best independent original execution
agrees with its representative by less than `stab_algo_threshold`, even when
Stab_algo and RSI pass. Component traversal continues; diagnostic values stay
independent. Use `require_reference_agreement=FALSE` to disable this gate.

With explicit `reference_bootstrap=TRUE`, a conditional bootstrap is run
only if both raw independent diagnostics already pass their strict thresholds,
agreement with the representative is below the algorithmic threshold, and the
execution does not improve its score. The representative is then fixed,
algorithmic stability is one by construction, and each bootstrap receives one
CEM descent from its projected labels. This conditional RSI measures agreement
with that reference. Raw independent values remain in the `_raw` columns;
`reference_bootstrap_applied` and `diagnostic_definition` identify the branch.
The default `reference_bootstrap=FALSE` keeps independent-only diagnostics.

## Inspect retained organizations

```{r representatives}
retained <- s[s$keep,,drop=FALSE]
representatives <- retained[!duplicated(retained$partition_id),,drop=FALSE]
representatives[,c("C","lambda","partition_id","REO")]
```

Many cells can represent the same partition. Present it once, together with
the cells where it is retained. This deduplication uses `partition_id` within
one result object. Do not compare these IDs across separate fitted objects.
Equal REO does not imply equal partitions, and distinct partitions need not
be nested.

```{r selected-partition}
if (nrow(representatives)>0) {
  q <- representatives[1,]
  CECplotPartition(g,C=q$C,lambda=q$lambda,x_var="x",y_var="y")
  print(table(CECextractPartition(g,q$C,q$lambda)))
} else {
  cat("No cell met these diagnostic requirements. Inspect the summary and budgets.\n")
}
```

The first representative is displayed only to illustrate access. The diagram
does not rank the retained partitions by scientific relevance. If a particular
application requires one decision, its external objective can guide the choice.
A rejected cell can also be inspected by supplying its coordinates explicitly.
The extraction helpers resolve to the nearest stored cell; they do not fit a
new model at an unstored coordinate. For an adaptive diagram they use the
containing rectangle and reject points outside the explored window.

## Change the penalty while keeping the candidates

```{r rescore}
g_bic <- CECrescoreGrid(g,penalty="bic")
cbind(CEC=g$summary$REO,CEC_BIC=g_bic$summary$REO)
stopifnot(identical(g$banks,g_bic$banks))
par(oma=c(0,0,0,4))
CECplotGrid(g_bic,main="Same banks with the BIC order penalty",
  reo_col=c("#0072B2","#D55E00","#009E73"))
```

This reuses EM fits, but it is more than changing a column in a table. Every
independent bank selects its winner again, and all diagnostics are recomputed.
The pooled representatives can therefore change along with their diagnostics.

The order penalty is `beta * (r-1)`, where
`beta=(d+1)*(d+2)*log(n)/(4*n)` for full Gaussian covariances.
It is added to the hard composite entropy, independently of `lambda`.
This differs from ordinary mixture-likelihood BIC.

## Adjust the diagnostic view

```{r selection}
keep <- CECselectStableLambdas(g,C=1,
  stab_algo_threshold=0.85,rsi_threshold=0.95,sat_threshold=0)
keep$stable_lambda
CECplotPath(g,C=1,type="summary")
```

The selector returns all retained lambdas for that C; it does not change
`g$summary$keep`. A plot can likewise use other display thresholds without
overwriting the fitted object. For a one-dimensional allocation path, pass
`lambda_stable_obj=keep` to `CECplotPath(type="partitions")` so its rejection
bands use the intended filter.

The RSI policy controls where both agreement averages are measured. Setting
`rsi_policy="nontrivial_unsaturated"` skips trivial and saturated cells.
For adaptive CEM, the pilot is constructed first, without L+B campaigns;
the policy then gates whole cell campaigns. Its default saturation band also
measures eligible trivial cells. With EM banks, as in this example, the banks
already exist and the policy gates agreement calculations.
Skipped direct values remain `NA`; a trivial cell is not automatically admitted.
For an EM grid, `CECrescoreGrid(g,rsi_policy="all")` broadens measurement
without repeating EM. It is unnecessary here because the original call
already measured all cells.

Adaptive diagrams default to connected-component traversal after freezing
the pilot. Cells with exactly the same partition and a shared edge form a
region. Eligible points are tested by increasing distance to its area-weighted
barycentre in `(log C, lambda)`. The first point passing both thresholds supplies
the region's diagnostic values for display and selection; the final saturation
filter is applied separately. These inherited values are a regional approximation.
`measured`, `diagnostic_origin`, `diagnostic_witness` and `_direct` columns
distinguish them from tests at individual points. Set
`adaptive_control=list(diagnostic_strategy="cells")` for pointwise coverage.
See `?CECadaptiveDiagram` for window calibration, refinement and stopping limits.

## Preserve the analysis

```{r saving, eval=FALSE}
saveRDS(g,"cec_none.rds")
saveRDS(g_bic,"cec_bic.rds")
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()),"sessionInfo.txt")

# Optional interactive exploration; stop the app to return to R.
CECexplore(g)
```

Use persistent paths for a real study. The RDS contains the fitting data,
controls, bootstrap indices, independent winners and candidates. Keep data
preprocessing code alongside it. The next guide explains computational
budgets, convergence records, checkpoints and the compatibility route.
